title: feat: add cohort_bind()
description:
Closes #76.

- `cohort_bind(..., links = NULL, separate = FALSE, study = NULL)` takes two or more named cohorts.
- `links` maps each cohort's subject ids to one id per person. Every subject needs a row; a missing one is an error that names it.
- `separate = TRUE` puts the cohort name and `_` in front of each id. It cannot be combined with `links`.
- New ids go into both tables, the subject rows of the QC and corrections logs, and loaded analysis tables with `subject_id`.
- `sample_map` and the three logs get a `source` column. Sample ids must be unique across cohorts. Subject rows of one person merge; a missing value is no conflict.
- Analysis, spec and path names that clash are errors. Dictionaries stack; one column described two ways is an error.
- A registered spec with `{subject_id}` in its path gets a warning when ids change, since its paths now resolve with the new ids.

Stacked on #99. Merge that one first, with a merge commit, and this diff shrinks to its own commits.

title: feat: load cohort-level tables lazily
description:
Closes #74.

- New format `parquet_dataset`, default reader `arrow::open_dataset`.
- `load_analysis(lazy = TRUE)` and `load_analyses(lazy = TRUE)` return the reader's object as it is and check `key_cols` against its column names. No row is read. Only the cohort level can load lazily; any other level is an error that says so.
- `cohort_filter()` filters a lazy arrow table by `subject_id` with `dplyr::filter()`, and it stays lazy. The issue proposed leaving it as it is, but then a filtered cohort would keep rows for subjects it removed.
- `translate()` skips a table that is not a data frame, with a warning to collect it first.
- arrow stays in Suggests; the tests skip without it.

Stacked on #98. Merge that one first, with a merge commit, and this diff shrinks to its own commits.

title: feat: add a column dictionary
description:
Closes #77.

- `Cohort` gets a `dictionary` property: `column`, `type` (`string` or `number`), `label`, `unit`, `values` (allowed values in order, separated by `|`).
- The tables stay text. The class validator checks the dictionary on every change: the column exists, a number column holds numbers, a string column holds only its values, and the id columns are strings. An error names the id and the column.
- `subjects()`, `samples()` and `as_coldata()` get `typed = TRUE`: number columns become numeric, string columns with values become factors in that level order.
- `cohort_dictionary()` returns the table. The study YAML reads and writes a `dictionary:` CSV.
- Labels and units stay in the table. No attributes go on columns.

Stacked on #97. Merge that one first, with a merge commit, and this diff shrinks to its own commits.

title: feat: read several manifest files into one cohort
description:
Closes #75, together with the missing-value change earlier in the stack.

- `read_manifest()` takes a character vector and stacks the files by column name. A column absent from one file is `NA` for its rows.
- A name on a path, as in `c(bulk_rna = "rna.csv")`, fills `assay` for a file that has none.
- A conflict across files names each value and its file, for example `R1 (sex: F in rna.csv, M in prot.csv)`. The one-file path is unchanged.
- The study YAML `manifest:` key accepts a list of `path` and `assay` entries. Corrections are applied to the stacked table. `write_study_yaml()` still writes one manifest.

Stacked on #96. Merge that one first, with a merge commit, and this diff shrinks to its own commits.

title: feat: keep the logs in the study YAML round trip
description:
Closes #78.

- `write_study_yaml()` writes each log that has rows as a CSV next to the manifest and lists it under `logs:` (`qc`, `derive`, `corrections`).
- Times are written in UTC as `2026-09-29T21:19:07Z`. Cutoffs are written as `young=0|old=40`. Both read back to their types.
- `Cohort` gets a `corrections` property and `cohort_new()` a `corrections` argument, so the audit survives `validate_manifest()`. `corrections_log()` accepts a cohort. `read_study_yaml()` keeps the audit of a `corrections:` file it applies.
- `cohort_read()` gives a cohort saved by 0.1.x each property added since. S7 errors on a missing property, so old files need this.
- `data/example_cohort.rda` is rebuilt from `data-raw/` for the new property.

Stacked on #95. Merge that one first, with a merge commit, and this diff shrinks to its own commits.

title: feat: record size, time and checksum in analysis_files()
description:
Closes #79.

- Each row of the files table gets `size` (bytes), `modified` and `sha256`.
- `sha256` is filled with `checksum = TRUE` on `load_analysis()` and `load_analyses()`, since a checksum reads every byte.
- A missing file has `NA` in all three.
- A folder gets the total size and the latest modified time of the files in it. A folder's own time does not change when a file inside it does. `sha256` stays `NA`.
- `cli (>= 3.2.0)` in Imports, the first version with `hash_file_sha256()`.

Stacked on #94. Merge that one first, with a merge commit, and this diff shrinks to its own commits.

title: feat: add a sample level to AnalysisSpec
description:
Closes #73.

- `level = "sample"`: one unit per sample of the spec's assay, in `sample_map` order.
- Path tokens `{sample_id}` and `{role}`. A sample with no role gives no `{role}` token, so a template that needs it stops with the usual unresolved-token error.
- Default `key_cols`: `subject_id` and `sample_id`.
- `cohort_filter()` trims a loaded table to the kept samples when its registered spec has `level = "sample"`. The registry decides, so a `sample_id` column in any other table is left alone.
- A sample dropped by `cohort_qc()` gives no unit. A flagged sample stays.
- One `.analysis_levels` constant now feeds both the class validator and `analysis_spec_new()`.

Stacked on #93. Merge that one first, with a merge commit, and this diff shrinks to its own commits.

title: feat: treat a missing subject value as no conflict
description:
Part of #75. A manifest stacked from several sheets often leaves a subject column empty in the sheet that does not carry it. In 0.1.1 that empty value counted as a conflict.

- `validate_manifest()` and `read_manifest()` get `missing_is_conflict = FALSE`. The one given value fills the subject row.
- Two different given values are still a conflict.
- `missing_is_conflict = TRUE` keeps the old check.
- Subject rows keep their first-seen order. The new internal `.collapse_subjects()` is reused by `cohort_bind()` later in the stack.

Stacked on #92. Merge that one first, with a merge commit, and this diff shrinks to its own commits.

title: fix: keep subject QC flags at the subject level
description:
`cohort_qc(scope = "subject", action = "flag")` wrote `qc_status` and `qc_reason` to `subject_tbl`, the same names the sample scope writes to `sample_map`. That broke three things:

- With both scopes flagged, `write_manifest()` and `write_study_yaml()` failed inside `dplyr::relocate()`.
- A subject flag alone moved to the samples after a write and a read, because `qc_status` is a known sample column.
- `samples(with_subjects = TRUE)` and `as_coldata()` got `qc_status.x` and `qc_status.y`.

The subject scope now writes `subject_qc_status` and `subject_qc_reason`. NEWS marks it as a breaking change, and `cohort_read()` renames the old columns in a cohort saved by 0.1.x.

The QC names were one case of a wider problem: any column other than `subject_id` in both tables made the join rename it to `.x` and `.y`. `cohort_derive()` could do it too. `write_manifest()` and `samples(with_subjects = TRUE)` now stop with an error that names the column, and `cohort_derive()` refuses a name used at the other level.

The branch also has one commit that regenerates NAMESPACE with roxygen2 8.1.0, so later branches do not carry that noise.

Stacked on #91. Merge that one first, with a merge commit, and this diff shrinks to its own commits.

title: chore: start the development version
description:
0.1.1 is on CRAN, and `DESCRIPTION` on `main` still said 0.1.1. The weekly cran job failed on the last two Mondays with "Insufficient package version (submitted: 0.1.1, existing: 0.1.1)". Nothing else was wrong.

- Version is now 0.1.1.9000, with a development heading in NEWS.
- The incoming pretest shows "Version contains large components" for every development version. cran.yml allows that line, so the job stays green between releases. A submission must drop the suffix, and CONTRIBUTING now says so and lists the release steps.
- The test that compares DESCRIPTION with CITATION.cff now compares only the first three parts of the version. The cite box keeps the last release (0.1.1) while DESCRIPTION carries 0.1.1.9000. At a release the full versions match again.
- Both READMEs get a CRAN badge, and installation starts with `install.packages("biocohort")`. GitHub and r-universe stay for the development version.

description:
Section names now match the other packages, so a reader who knows one README can find their way around the next.

| Was | Now |

| A first cohort | Usage |
| Learn more | Documentation |
| Citing biocohort | Citation |

title: docs: show a cohort on the front page
description:
## The front page showed nothing

`README.md` described the package for ninety lines and never showed it. It now
opens a manifest and builds a cohort in the first screen, then says why.

The Motivation section was 32 lines and is now 14. One paragraph of it read:

> It is not just for genomics, even though early drafts of the docs read that
> way.

A reader cannot see earlier drafts. The `MultiAssayExperiment` comparison stays,
because that is the question a Bioconductor user actually arrives with.

## Corrections

| Where | Problem |
| --- | --- |
| Citing | Named 0.1.0 as the version to pin; the package is 0.1.1 |
| Citing | Said every release is archived; Zenodo holds 0.1.0 only |
| Repository layout | Demonstrated package commands with `devtools` |
| Installation | Explained the `pkg-r` suffix directly under a command carrying it |

## pkg-r/README.md

This is the page r-universe renders, and it sent readers to the root README for
the reason the package exists. It carries that reason itself now.

It also gained a licence badge and a licence line, and lost the instructions for
building the pkgdown site locally, which are contributor material.

## Badges

Both files gained a licence badge, matching the other packages.

title: docs: make the badge row honest and dependable
description:
The DOI badge came from `zenodo.org`, whose badge endpoints are not dependable. Measured over five requests each:

```
zenodo.org/badge/DOI/<doi>.svg     timed out x5, 15 seconds each
zenodo.org/badge/<repo-id>.svg     403 x5
img.shields.io/badge/DOI-...       200 x5, 0.08 to 0.16 seconds
```

That is why a DOI badge often fails to appear on first load and then shows up on a refresh. The browser gives up waiting, and a later cached fetch succeeds.

The replacement is served by shields and renders `DOI: 10.5281/zenodo....`:

```markdown
[![DOI](https://img.shields.io/badge/DOI-10.5281%2Fzenodo.21731864-1682D4)](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21731864)
```

The slash becomes `%2F`, and `1682D4` is Zenodo's blue, so it still reads as a DOI badge.

It is also static, which fixes a second problem. `zenodo.org/badge/<repo-id>.svg` resolves to whatever Zenodo currently thinks is newest, while the link stays pinned to whatever was written, so after a release the image and the link can name different DOIs. With the DOI in both halves they cannot disagree.

## Lifecycle

Added, because every package should say what state it is in and none of them did. The stage follows CRAN: a package accepted there has users who can be broken by a change.

## Checked

The DOI resolves, and the badge renders, rather than being assumed.

title: ci: run Windows and macOS on every pull request, full matrix weekly
description:
Until now a pull request ran one Ubuntu R-release check and the other four configurations were manual only. That gate was aimed at the two slow jobs, Ubuntu R-devel (27 min) and R-oldrel-1 (14 min), which build Bioconductor from source. Windows (3 to 4 min) and macOS (1 to 3 min) install binaries and were swept up with them for no reason.

Now a pull request runs R-release on Ubuntu, Windows, and macOS in parallel, so the wait is unchanged, and the full matrix runs every Monday at the same slot as the cran workflow as well as on demand. Windows is the platform most likely to behave differently (path separators, file locking) and CRAN's pretest runs it too.

This PR is its own test: three R-CMD-check jobs should appear below instead of one.

title: chore: bump version to 0.1.1 for the CRAN resubmission
description:
0.1.0 was never published, so this is the number the resubmission goes out under. CRAN prefers a higher number on every submission, and it keeps the CRAN tarball, the GitHub release, and the Zenodo version DOI describing the same commit. Nothing but documentation changed since 0.1.0; NEWS.md lists it, and cran-comments.md opens as a resubmission and records the win-builder R-devel result on the fixed package (1 NOTE, new submission plus the three known words).

After merge: submit biocohort_0.1.1.tar.gz, and once CRAN accepts, tag v0.1.1 so Zenodo mints the matching version DOI.

title: docs: answer the CRAN pretest and add a cran workflow
description:
CRAN's incoming pretest bounced 0.1.0 on 2026-09-10 with two NOTEs. This branch answers both, adds what a human reviewer asks for next, rewrites the Description field, and adds a workflow so the pretest's checks run here before a submission instead of at it.

## What the pretest flagged

- **Invalid file URIs.** `?biocohort` linked the three articles by a relative path that exists only on the website, and `pkg-r/README.md` linked `../CONTRIBUTING.md`, which is not in the tarball. The help page now names the articles as `vignette("name", package = "biocohort")` calls (pkgdown still links them, checked by building the page), and the README links CONTRIBUTING.md by URL.
- **`liftover_rtracklayer` example over 5 s.** The time is rtracklayer loading, 4.1 s here and 6.0 s on CRAN's Debian box. The example is in `\donttest{}` now. R only times the pass that skips donttest; the `--as-cran` second pass still runs it, and did.
- **Possibly misspelled words.** The Description rewrite drops `backends` and `pluggable`. `omics`, `liftover`, and `ortholog` stay and are explained in cran-comments.md.

## What a reviewer asks for next

- `translation_report()`'s example was three commented lines. It is code now.
- Examples added for `translate()` on a cohort, `load_analyses()`, `cohort_read()`, `register_liftover_backend()`, `register_ortholog_backend()`, `liftover_vcf()` (as `\dontrun{}`, it needs CrossMap and a reference genome), and the `Study`, `Subject`, `Cohort`, `AnalysisSpec`, and `TranslationResult` constructors. All run and print sensible output.
- Help pages that still pointed at the deprecated `orthologize()` point at `translate()`.
- cran-comments.md is rewritten as a resubmission. The old version claimed CrossMap was installed on the checking machine. It is not.

## Why the local check never showed any of this

The plain check leaves the CRAN incoming checks off, and the file URI check is a separate flag the pretest sets. The spell check needs aspell, which Windows lacks. The new `cran` workflow turns all of those on, installs aspell, and fails on any NOTE the pretest would not accept. Its filter was tested against the real failing log (fails, listing the four URIs), the fixed log (passes), CRAN's own spelling NOTE (flags only the two removed words), and the timing NOTE (fails). Pull requests run it on R-release; Mondays and manual runs use R-devel, as the pretest does.

## Verification

`R CMD check --as-cran` with the incoming, remote URL, and file URI checks enabled: 0 errors, 0 warnings, and only the two known NOTEs (new submission, the Windows `NULL` folder). The tarball is rebuilt. win-builder R-devel has been sent the same tarball for the aspell check; the result goes to the maintainer address.

Version stays 0.1.0, since that version was never published.

title: docs: add r-universe install instructions and badge to both READMEs
description:
biocohort is now registered on samuelbharti.r-universe.dev (subdir: pkg-r), matching bioclients/biobouncer/plotomics. Adds the r-universe badge and `install.packages("biocohort", repos = "https://samuelbharti.r-universe.dev")` install line to both READMEs, and the DOI badge to pkg-r/README.md to match the root README's badge set.

r-universe hasn't finished its first build yet as of this PR (checked via the package API), but the badge and install line are correct regardless and will resolve once it does.

title: docs: add inst/CITATION so citation("biocohort") includes the Zenodo DOI
description:
Following up on #64: `citation("biocohort")` did not actually include the Zenodo DOI, since R only reads `CITATION.cff` for GitHub's own "Cite this repository" button, not for its own `citation()` output. Without an `inst/CITATION` file, R falls back to auto-generating a bare citation from `DESCRIPTION` alone.

Verified by building the tarball, installing it, and running `citation("biocohort")` before and after: the DOI (`doi:10.5281/zenodo.22685057`) now appears in both the text and BibTeX forms. Full `R CMD check --as-cran` still comes back with only the two known, explained NOTEs.

title: docs: add Zenodo DOI to CITATION.cff and README
description: v0.1.0 is now archived on Zenodo (concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22685057, version DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22685058). Adds both to `CITATION.cff` (so `citation("biocohort")` and GitHub's "Cite this repository" button pick them up), a DOI badge, and a "Citing biocohort" section in the README, matching the pattern bioclients already uses.

title: chore: bring main up to date with dev
description: Final dev sync before retiring dev as an integration branch: removes the stale status line and syncs the root LICENSE copyright with Posit, and makes the pkgdown site light-only to match the logo's parchment palette. Going forward, feature branches PR directly into main; dev is left in place but unused.

title: ci: drop dev, PRs target main directly, full R-CMD-check matrix goes manual-only
description:
Retires `dev` as an integration branch. Every workflow now triggers on pull requests into `main` only (`r.yml`, `lint.yml`, `pr-title.yml`, `secret-scan.yml`, `coverage.yml`, `pkgdown.yml`), dependabot targets `main`, and `CONTRIBUTING.md` describes the new flow.

R CMD check's full 5-platform matrix (the 20-30 minute devel/oldrel-1 builds) previously ran automatically on every PR into `main`, back when that only happened at a deliberate dev-to-main sync. Since every PR now targets `main` directly, that matrix is demoted to manual-only (`workflow_dispatch`, run from the Actions tab) so routine PRs stay fast; trigger it deliberately before a release or a CRAN submission.

pkgdown's `/dev/` preview deploy step is removed along with its trigger; the next deploy to `main` will clean the old `/dev/` pages off `gh-pages`.

`dev` itself is left in place, just unused going forward. A separate change updates the branch ruleset to match (protect `dev` from deletion/force-push without requiring pull requests into it, since nothing will target it anymore).

title: chore: make the pkgdown site light-only, matching the logo's parchment palette
description: Removes the dark-mode toggle (`light-switch: false`) and sets the site's background/foreground to the same parchment (`#f3ecdd`) and dark aubergine (`#2a1a2d`) as the hex logo, so the docs site and the logo read as one object regardless of visitor theme preference. Built the site locally and rendered the home page and a reference page to confirm contrast and legibility before landing this.

title: docs: remove stale status line, sync root LICENSE copyright with Posit
description: Removes the root README's status line, which still said 0.1.0.9000/not released after the version bump. Also fixes the root `LICENSE` file, which was missed during the earlier LICENSE sync: it still only listed Samuel Bharti as copyright holder, while `pkg-r/LICENSE`/`LICENSE.md` and `DESCRIPTION`'s `Authors@R` already credit Posit Software, PBC as `cph`. The root file is the one GitHub actually reads for license detection, so this was the more visible copy to have missed.

title: chore: bring main up to date with dev
description: Syncs main with everything merged to dev since the last sync: the review-driven feature batch (cohort_qc, cohort_groups/cohort_contrasts, cohort_derive, a default parquet reader), CRAN-readiness follow-ups (missing examples, LICENSE copyright sync, cran-comments.md), a review pass that found and fixed real bugs (cli pluralization, a reason-append edge case, an invalid-cutoff crash), and the version bump to 0.1.0 for the first release.

title: chore: bump version to 0.1.0 for the first release
description: Drops the `.9000` dev suffix now that the package is ready for its first release: `DESCRIPTION`, `CITATION.cff`, and `NEWS.md`'s heading and intro. Also removes the now-resolved "Version contains large components" note from `cran-comments.md` (confirmed gone from a fresh `R CMD check --as-cran` run).

title: fix: fix pluralization and cutoff/reason edge cases in cohort_qc() and cohort_derive()
description:
Found during a deep review pass before syncing to `main`:

- `cohort_qc()`'s unknown-id error and `cohort_derive()`'s non-numeric-value error always printed singular ("id" not "ids") for multiple ids, because a length-1 variable placed before `{?s}` in the message defeated cli's auto-pluralization. Fixed with `cli::qty()`.
- `cohort_qc()`'s reason-append logic could silently drop a legitimately new reason if it matched a semicolon-delimited fragment of an earlier reason. Simplified to only skip an exact full-string repeat.
- `cohort_derive()` crashed with a raw, confusing error on a `cutoffs` value of `-Inf`. Now rejected up front with a clear message.

Also adds the 4 new functions from the last 4 PRs (`cohort_qc`, `cohort_groups`/`cohort_contrasts`, `cohort_derive`) to `?biocohort` and both READMEs, since none of them were mentioned anywhere outside the auto-generated function reference.

title: docs: add examples for the three undocumented functions, sync LICENSE copyright, add cran-comments.md
description: Adds guarded examples to `liftover_rtracklayer()`, `liftover_crossmap()`, and `ortholog_babelgene()` (previously the only three exported functions with no `@examples`). Syncs `LICENSE`/`LICENSE.md`'s copyright holder with `DESCRIPTION`'s `Authors@R` (Posit Software, PBC is listed there as `cph` but was missing from the license text). Adds `cran-comments.md` for the eventual submission. Also fixes a circular line in `pkg-r/README.md` (it linked to its own documentation URL) and matches its wording to the root README's "Motivation" section.

title: feat: add cohort_derive() for cutoff-derived columns with provenance
description: Adds `cohort_derive()`, which bins an existing numeric column at one or more named cutoffs and writes the result as a new column on `subject_tbl` or `sample_map` (never inventing a label for a bin the caller did not name). `derive_log()` reads the provenance every call appends to a new, durable `Cohort@derived` property, following the same not-cleared-by-`cohort_filter()` pattern as `cohort_qc()`'s `@qc`.

title: feat: add cohort_groups() and cohort_contrasts() for pairwise group comparisons
description:
Adds `cohort_groups()`, which groups a cohort's subjects by one or more `subject_tbl` columns and returns one row per combination that actually occurs (never an invented, unobserved combination), and `cohort_contrasts()`, which enumerates every pairwise contrast between those groups.

Both are pure reads: no cohort mutation, no new `Cohort` property. `cohort_contrasts()` accepts either a Cohort directly or the tibble `cohort_groups()` already returned, and its output composes directly with `cohort_filter(cohort, subject_ids = ...)`.

title: feat: infer species, translate mixed-species cohorts, unify feature id
description:
## Description
orthologize() required from even though the cohort already knows every subject's species, translated a whole mixed-species cohort with one from, and used two different row-key column names between the liftover and ortholog backends.

## Changes Made
- translate() is the new primary name. orthologize() is now a thin alias that warns once per session (cli's built-in once-per-session frequency control) and calls translate().
- Cohort translation infers from from subject_tbl$species: used directly for a single-species cohort, resolved per analysis (and per subject, when the analysis table has a subject_id column) for a cohort with more than one species. An explicit from not among the cohort's species now warns instead of translating silently.
- A mixed-species translation combines the per-species results into one TranslationResult: from becomes a vector of the species involved, and mapped/unmapped gain a .source_species column.
- chain can be a named list (one chain file per source species) for a mixed-species cohort with an interval analysis, instead of only a single path.
- .liftover_id and .ortholog_id are unified into one .feature_id key in both backends, both built-in implementations, and the docs. TranslationResult's docs no longer call gene-level translation a future feature.
- ortholog_babelgene() gains a cache argument: a TSV file of prior from/to/id_type/input_id/target_id lookups, read before querying babelgene and appended to after.

## Testing

## Description

- as_coldata(cohort, assay, samples =, rownames =, ref =) returns a base data.frame with sample_id row names, ready for SummarizedExperiment/DESeqDataSet colData. samples orders and checks against the cohort; ref relevels a factor column (for example genotype = "WT") before a differential analysis.
- join_metadata(object, cohort, assay =, by =, col =) adds cohort metadata onto a data.frame (left join), a SummarizedExperiment (colData), or a Seurat object (meta.data), matched by sample id. An id in object that does not match a cohort sample is an error naming it.

## Description
A manifest entry point that reads CSV, TSV, or Excel with every column forced to character, a reshaper for wide sample sheets, a writer that turns a cohort back into one long file, and a save/read pair for a cohort as a file.

- manifest_from_wide(x, id_cols) turns a one-row-per-subject wide table into the long format validate_manifest() expects, given a small table of (column, assay, role).
- write_manifest(x, path) joins a Cohort's or validate_manifest()'s tables back into one long file, subject_id first, then subject columns, then sample columns.

## Description

Analysis loading now follows the spec's assay. A subject-level spec enumerates only subjects that have a sample of that assay. A pair-level spec pairs only within that assay, with the roles and separator the spec declares. Both warn and return empty tables when nothing matches. `format`, `reader`, and `key_cols` become optional on `analysis_spec_new()` with sensible defaults, and `key_cols` gets a job: `load_analysis()` checks the columns after reading.

Roadmap items 10, 11, 12, and 19.

## Changes Made

- `sample_pairs()` gains `sep = "__"` for the `pair_id` separator.
- `AnalysisSpec` gains `tumor_role`, `normal_role`, and `pair_sep`. `analysis_spec_new()` exposes them with the same defaults.
- `analysis_spec_new()`: `format` defaults from the `path_template` extension, `reader` from `format` (csv, tsv, txt, rds), `key_cols` by `level`. `reader` and `key_cols` move after the defaulted arguments.
- `load_analysis()`: subject and pair units come only from the spec assay. Errors when no reader resolves. Errors naming the missing columns when a file lacks a `key_cols` column.

title: Analysis feature loading: paths -> loaded tables (load_analysis/load_analyses)
description:
## Summary

The final structural piece of the translation pipeline: read analysis feature tables **from disk** using each `AnalysisSpec`'s `path_template` + `root_key` + `reader`, so a cohort can go *paths → loaded tables → translated* in three calls.

### What's here
- **`load_analysis(cohort, spec, reader = NULL)`** — resolves the spec's `path_template` for each unit implied by its `level`:
  - `subject` → one file per subject (`{subject_id}`)
  - `pair` → one file per tumor/normal pair (`{pair_id}`, `{tumor_sample_id}`, `{normal_sample_id}`), derived via `sample_pairs()`
  - `cohort` → one file
  
  Reads existing files via the spec's `reader` (a base function or `"pkg::fun"`), row-binds them, and annotates rows with provenance keys (`subject_id`/`pair_id`).
- **`load_analyses(cohort, ...)`** — populates `cohort@analyses` for all registered specs and records per-analysis file manifests.
- **`analysis_files(cohort)`** — retrieve those manifests (resolved paths + whether each existed).

### Honest by design
Missing files are **reported (warning + manifest), never silently dropped**. Unresolved path tokens and unknown readers error with actionable messages.

### The pipeline now composes
```r
cohort |>
  load_analyses() |>                          # paths -> feature tables
  orthologize(to = "human", from = "rat",     # translate every analysis
              chain = "ratToHuman.chain")
```

### Testing
- `devtools::test()`: 208 pass, 0 fail, **0 skipped** — loader tested end-to-end with real temp files and real readers (`read.csv`, `readRDS`, custom fn) across subject and pair levels, missing-file + error paths, and a `load_analyses() -> orthologize()` integration.
- `R CMD check` (vignettes deferred to CI): 0 errors, 0 warnings, 1 pre-existing NOTE.

title: Cohort-level orthologize(): translate a whole cohort across species
description:
## Summary

The capstone of the translation layer: `orthologize()` now works on a whole **`Cohort`**, not just individual feature tables. This realizes the original vision — *"create an orthologous object from one class to another"* — at the cohort level.

### What's here
- **`orthologize(cohort, to, from, ...)`** — translates every registered analysis according to its `AnalysisSpec` and returns a **new, target-species `Cohort`**. Subjects and the sample map are unchanged (same biological subjects, re-expressed in another species' coordinate/gene space); each analysis's feature table is translated.
- **`AnalysisSpec` gains `feature_type` (`"interval"`/`"gene"`), `gene_col`, `id_type`** (all optional, validated) — these drive automatic per-assay dispatch: interval → liftover, gene → ortholog.
- **`translation_report(cohort)`** — retrieve the per-analysis `TranslationResult`s (including unmapped features and stats) recorded during translation.
- One verb, two input types: feature table → `TranslationResult`; cohort → translated `Cohort`.

### Honest by design
Analyses without a registered spec or without a `feature_type` are **skipped with a warning, never guessed**. Interval analyses require a `chain`. Nothing is faked.

### Testing
- `devtools::test()`: 186 pass, 0 fail, **0 skipped** locally — cohort orchestration covered via mock backends (deterministic) plus a real babelgene gene-analysis translation (TP53→Trp53 inside a cohort); skip/error paths and the new spec validation are tested.
- `R CMD check` (vignettes deferred to CI): 0 errors, 0 warnings, 1 pre-existing NOTE.

### Remaining roadmap
Feature **loading** from disk (read VCF/peak/expression files into per-assay tables via `AnalysisSpec` path templates + readers) so a cohort can be translated straight from file paths. This PR translates the in-memory feature tables held in `cohort@analyses`; wiring the readers is the next step — and the natural point to run real-data validation.

title: Gene-level ortholog backend (babelgene) — completes orthologize() dispatch
description:
## Summary

Implements the **`ortholog`** half of `orthologize()` (the liftover half shipped in #9). Gene-level features now translate across species, so `orthologize()` is a complete modality dispatcher: coordinates → liftover, genes → orthologs.

- **`ortholog_genes(features, from, to, gene_col, id_type, backend)`** — gene-level cross-species mapping returning a `TranslationResult` (mapped + unmapped + stats), exactly mirroring `liftover_intervals()`.
- **Pluggable backends** via `register_ortholog_backend()` / `ortholog_backends()`; default **`ortholog_babelgene()`** uses the offline `babelgene` package. Model→model pairs (e.g. rat→mouse) are pivoted through human, since babelgene is human-centric.
- **`orthologize(strategy = "ortholog")`** now routes here; `backend` defaults per-strategy (`rtracklayer` for liftover, `babelgene` for ortholog).

### Dependencies
`babelgene` added to **Suggests**, guarded at runtime. It's offline (ships ortholog data) — no network calls.

### Testing
- `devtools::test()`: 164 pass, 0 fail, **0 skipped** locally — the real babelgene adapter runs end-to-end (TP53/MYC → Trp53/Myc human→mouse, plus a mouse→rat pivot-through-human); orchestrator covered via a mock backend.
- `R CMD check` (vignettes deferred to CI): 0 errors, 0 warnings, 1 pre-existing NOTE.

### Still ahead (per roadmap)
Cohort-level `orthologize(cohort, to = "human")` that loads feature data per assay and dispatches liftover/ortholog automatically — needs the feature-loading layer, deliberately not faked here.

title: Experimental cross-species translation: liftover + orthologize() scaffold
description:
## Summary

First cut of the cross-species **translation** layer discussed in #7 — the genuine unmet-need wedge (vs. re-implementing a cohort container). Coordinate features (variants/peaks/intervals) translate across assemblies/species via chain-file liftover; the API shape for gene-level orthologs is reserved but stubbed.

### What's here
- **`orthologize(x, to, strategy = c("liftover","ortholog"), ...)`** — modality dispatcher. `liftover` is functional; `ortholog` is a documented placeholder (planned via `orthogene`/`babelgene`).
- **`liftover_intervals()`** — translate intervals via a chain file; returns a **`TranslationResult`** that keeps *mapped* **and** *unmapped* features so loss is never silent.
- **Pluggable backends** — `register_liftover_backend()` / `liftover_backends()`. Ships an R-native **`rtracklayer`** default and a **`crossmap`** adapter; **`liftover_vcf()`** wraps CrossMap's allele-aware variant liftover (the thing plain interval liftover can't do).
- **`TranslationResult`** S7 class + `print` + **`translation_stats()`** (input/mapped/unmapped/multi).

### Deliberately honest about limits
Cross-species liftover is synteny-bound and lossy — the result type forces you to see the unmapped fraction. The `ortholog` strategy is intentionally not faked.

### Dependencies
`rtracklayer`/`GenomicRanges`/`IRanges`/`S4Vectors` are **Suggests**, guarded at runtime (pak resolves Bioc on CI). CrossMap is optional, noted in `SystemRequirements`.

### Testing
- `devtools::test()`: 144 pass, 0 fail, **0 skipped** locally — the real `rtracklayer` adapter runs end-to-end against a synthetic chain; the orchestrator is covered via a mock backend; CrossMap-absent path asserts a clear error.
- `R CMD check` (vignettes deferred to CI): 0 errors, 0 warnings, 1 pre-existing NOTE.

### How to try it on real data
`liftover_vcf(vcf, chain, ref_fasta, to = "human")` with a rat→human chain, then diff against your manual CrossMap output.

Marked **experimental** — merging the scaffold so the API can stabilize while the ortholog backend and Cohort-level orchestration land in follow-ups.

title: Add generic sample_pairs() helper for tumor/normal pairing
description:
## Summary

Closes the last loose end from the 0.3.0 manifest generalization (#7): the `AnalysisSpec` framing still leaned on the old WES-specific tumor/normal `pair_id`.

- **New `sample_pairs()`** — derives tumor/normal (case/control) pairs on demand from the long-format `sample_map`, assay-agnostic. Within each `subject_id` × `assay`, every tumor-role sample is paired with every normal-role sample. Returns `subject_id`, `assay`, `tumor_sample_id`, `normal_sample_id`, `pair_id`; role labels configurable via `tumor_role`/`normal_role`.
- **Reframed `AnalysisSpec`** — `level = "pair"` and the `{tumor_sample_id}`/`{normal_sample_id}`/`{pair_id}` path tokens now reference `sample_pairs()` generically instead of a stored WES pair.
- Re-added a generic **Pair** concept to the glossary + naming-conventions vignettes, listed the helper in the package overview, and added a NEWS feature entry.

## Testing
